objects.definition: typedef unsigned int khint32_t;
objects.description: 32-bit unsigned integer type used by khash for hashing and indexing on platforms where unsigned int is 32 bits. Exact underlying base type depends on limits macros; this branch selects unsigned int.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned long khint32_t;
objects.description: Alternative definition for khint32_t when unsigned long is 32 bits (platform-dependent). Note: Only one khint32_t actually takes effect based on UINT_MAX/ULONG_MAX. This duplicate documents the conditional variant.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned long khint64_t;
objects.description: 64-bit unsigned integer type used by khash for 64-bit keys when unsigned long equals unsigned long long (platform-dependent).

objects.definition: typedef unsigned long long khint64_t;
objects.description: Alternative definition for khint64_t when unsigned long is not 64 bits. Only one of the khint64_t typedefs is active depending on platform limits.

objects.definition: typedef khint32_t khint_t;
objects.description: Index/size type for khash tables. Typically a 32-bit unsigned integer aliasing khint32_t. Used for bucket indices, counts, and return values of kh_* APIs.

objects.definition: typedef khint_t khiter_t;
objects.description: Iterator/index type for traversing khash buckets. Alias of khint_t. Returned by kh_get/kh_put and compared against kh_end.

objects.definition: typedef const char *kh_cstr_t;
objects.description: Alias for const char* used as key type in string-key khash specializations.

Node header for a B-tree used by the kbtree macros. The bitfield indicates whether the node is internal (is_internal=1) or a leaf (0), and n stores the number of keys currently in the node. The actual key array and (for internal nodes) child pointers are stored inline after this header, with offsets computed by macros.
A position within a kbtree: x points to a node and i indexes into that node’s key/child slots. Used internally by iterators and traversal helpers.

Iterator state for traversing a kbtree. Maintains an explicit stack of kbpos_t entries up to KB_MAX_DEPTH and a current stack pointer p. Used with kb_itr_first/next/get macros generated per tree type.
Deprecated traversal stack frame used by legacy __kb_traverse macro. Similar to kbpos_t but intended for the old traversal API.

objects.definition:
#define __KAVL_ITR(suf, __scope, __type, __head, __cmp) \
	struct kavl_itr_##suf { \
		const __type *stack[KAVL_MAX_DEPTH], **top; \
	}; \
	__scope void kavl_itr_first_##suf(const __type *root, struct kavl_itr_##suf *itr) { \
		const __type *p; \
		for (itr->top = itr->stack - 1, p = root; p; p = p->__head.p[0]) \
			*++itr->top = p; \
	} \
	__scope int kavl_itr_find_##suf(const __type *root, const __type *x, struct kavl_itr_##suf *itr) { \
		const __type *p = root; \
		itr->top = itr->stack - 1; \
		while (p != 0) { \
			int cmp; \
			*++itr->top = p; \
			cmp = __cmp(x, p); \
			if (cmp < 0) p = p->__head.p[0]; \
			else if (cmp > 0) p = p->__head.p[1]; \
			else break; \
		} \
		return p? 1 : 0; \
	} \
	__scope int kavl_itr_next_bidir_##suf(struct kavl_itr_##suf *itr, int dir) { \
		const __type *p; \
		if (itr->top < itr->stack) return 0; \
		dir = !!dir; \
		p = (*itr->top)->__head.p[dir]; \
		if (p) { /* go down */ \
			for (; p; p = p->__head.p[!dir]) \
				*++itr->top = p; \
			return 1; \
		} else { /* go up */ \
			do { \
				p = *itr->top--; \
			} while (itr->top >= itr->stack && p == (*itr->top)->__head.p[dir]); \
			return itr->top < itr->stack? 0 : 1; \
		} \
	}
objects.description: Per-suffix iterator struct generated by the __KAVL_ITR macro. Each instantiation defines a distinct struct type named struct kavl_itr_<suf> that holds a traversal stack for in-order iteration over a specific tree of nodes of type __type. The struct contains a fixed-size stack of node pointers and a top pointer. Created/used by the iterator helper functions generated alongside it.

Stack frame used internally by ks_introsort_* for non-recursive quicksort/introsort. Holds subarray bounds (left/right as void* pointers later cast to element-pointer type) and remaining recursion depth.

objects.definition: typedef const char *ksstr_t;
objects.description: Alias for const char*. Used by the KSORT_INIT_STR specialization to sort C strings via strcmp.
Growable string buffer with length l, capacity m, and data pointer s. Used for names, comments, sequences, and qualities. Caller manages memory; commonly resized by kseq/ks helpers.

Resizable string buffer with length l, capacity m, and data pointer s. Non-opaque; callers may read/write fields directly. Initialize with {0,0,NULL}. Buffer is heap-allocated and must be freed by freeing s (or via ks_release to transfer ownership).
Auxiliary state used by kstrtok for tokenization without modifying the input. Holds separator table, state flags, and pointer to end of current token.

objects.definition: typedef char *kgets_func(char *, int, void *);
objects.description: Function type compatible with fgets-like readers used by kgetline. Implementations read up to size-1 chars into buffer from stream-like user data and return buffer or NULL on EOF/error.

objects.definition: typedef double (*kmin_f)(int, double*, void*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for multivariate objective functions used by optimizers. The function takes dimensionality n, a pointer to an n-length vector x, and an opaque user data pointer, returning the objective value as double.

objects.definition: typedef double (*kmin1_f)(double, void*);
objects.description: Function pointer type for one-dimensional objective functions. The function takes a scalar x and an opaque user data pointer, returning the objective value as double.

objects.definition: #define KE_EXCESS_ITER (-1)
objects.description: Macro constant representing the error code returned when an algorithm exceeds the maximum number of iterations. This is a preprocessor macro, not a true type; included here only to note there are no user-defined types in this header.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned kgint_t;
objects.description: Unsigned integer typedef used as the key/index type for graph vertices (and packed arc keys). Acts as the canonical integer type carried through the kgraph macros.

State container for a small 128-bit xorshift-like random number generator. It holds two 64-bit state words used by the PRNG functions in this header. Must be initialized (e.g., via kr_srand_r) before use.

objects.description: Macro that defines a per-suffix iterator struct type struct krmq_itr_<suf> used to traverse the tree in-order (forward/backward). It holds an explicit stack of node pointers and a top pointer for traversal state. The exact name depends on the suffix provided to KRMQ_INIT/KRMQ_INIT2.

objects.definition: #define krmq_itr_t(suf) struct krmq_itr_##suf
objects.description: Macro alias that names the iterator struct produced by __KRMQ_ITR for a given suffix. This is an aliasing macro; the underlying defined type is struct krmq_itr_<suf>.

State object for parsing command-line options with ketopt(). Tracks current index, last option, argument pointer, and long-option index, plus internal iterator state. Initialize with KETOPT_INIT before first use. The struct is fully defined here; fields i, pos, n_args are internal.

Descriptor for a long option used by ketopt(). name is the long option string (without leading dashes), has_arg uses ko_no_argument/ko_required_argument/ko_optional_argument, and val is the code returned when this option is matched.

Opaque pointer used as a handle for a for-loop thread pool created by kt_forpool_init and consumed by kt_forpool and kt_forpool_destroy. The concrete struct type is not defined in this header; only an opaque void* is exposed.

Opaque-ish file-like handle supporting local, FTP, and HTTP access. Tracks file descriptor, current offset, and protocol-specific state (FTP control/data info, HTTP path/host). Used by knet_open/knet_dopen to create, knet_read to read, knet_seek to reposition (lazy for FTP), and knet_close to destroy. I/O is currently unbuffered per comment. Details of lifetime management: created by knet_open or knet_dopen and must be released with knet_close.

Opaque-ish BGZF file handle used by the BGZF compressed I/O API. Holds mode and compression parameters, current block state and offsets, buffers for compressed/uncompressed data, an optional cache, and an underlying file handle. Intended to be created/opened via bgzf_open/bgzf_dopen and closed via bgzf_close. Internal fields should be treated as implementation details.

Resizable string type with length l, capacity m, and char buffer s. Used by bgzf_getline to return lines. Memory ownership and growth are managed by the caller; must be initialized by the user before use (e.g., zeroed fields).

objects.definition: struct kurl_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a URL-backed I/O stream. The struct is only forward-declared here, indicating an internal, private implementation managed via the provided API for opening, reading, seeking, and closing. Memory ownership and lifecycle are controlled by kurl_open/kurl_dopen and kurl_close.

Options for opening URLs, notably credentials for S3 access. Fields: s3keyid and s3secretkey provide explicit credentials; s3key_fn points to a file containing credentials. Exact precedence/validation is not specified in this header.

objects.definition: typedef kurl_t knetFile;
objects.description: Alias type for kurl_t used for backward compatibility with the knetfile API. It is an opaque handle identical to kurl_t; lifecycle is managed by the kurl_* functions (macros map knet_* to kurl_*).

Node in a lightweight JSON-like tree. The bitfield packs a 3-bit type (KSON_TYPE_*) and a 61-bit count/length. For array/object nodes (bracket/brace), v.child points to an array of child node pointers with count n; for scalar string-like nodes, v.str holds the string value, and n commonly encodes the length/auxiliary count. key is present for keyed members (object fields).
Top-level KSON document handle holding the root node and the total number of allocated nodes. Owns the tree allocated by kson_parse and is freed by kson_destroy.

Hidden Markov Model parameter set: sizes (m symbols, n states), transition matrix a (n x n), emission probabilities e (n x m), start transition vector a0 (n), and an auxiliary matrix ae used to accelerate backward/posterior computations via hmm_pre_backward().

Per-sequence working data for HMM inference: sequence length L, flags/status, observed sequence seq, forward matrix f, backward matrix b, scaling or normalization vector s, Viterbi path v, and posterior-decoded state path p.

Expected sufficient statistics container for EM: dimensions (m, n), accumulated Q0 term, expected transition counts A (n x n), expected emission counts E (n x m), and expected start transitions A0 (n). Used by EM-related functions such as hmm_expect, hmm_add_expect, hmm_Q, hmm_Q0.

Goodness-of-fit helper structure with length l, observed counts obs, and threshold values thr. Not constructed by any API function in this header; likely used for GOF analyses in implementation files.

objects.definition: struct _kswq_t;
objects.description: Opaque forward-declared query profile type used by ksw_align to cache/precompute scoring profile for a query sequence. The actual structure layout is intentionally hidden; users manage it via ksw_align which allocates and may free it as documented. Details of fields are unknown in this header.

Result container for sequence alignment outcomes returned by ksw_align. Holds best score and end coordinates; optionally second-best score/position and start coordinates when enabled via flags. Values may be -1 when not computed; score may saturate depending on flags.

Node structure for an NHX-like tree: stores the parent index, number of children, array of child indices, node name, and a numeric value (likely branch length or other annotation). Allocation/ownership of child and name are not documented here; they are presumably managed by the parser/formatter functions. Details such as lifetime and memory ownership are unknown from this header.

A simple dynamic string buffer: l is current length, m is capacity, and s is the character buffer. The macro KSTRING_T is defined as an alias for kstring_t. No allocation helpers are defined in this header; the buffer is likely managed by caller-provided utilities elsewhere.

functions.name: kv_roundup32
functions.description: Macro that rounds an unsigned integer lvalue up to the next power-of-two-like capacity using a bit-twiddling sequence. It decrements the value first, propagates highest set bit across lower bits, then increments, effectively computing a ceiling to the next power of two (for 32-bit width). Intended for sizing vector capacity.
requirements: Argument x must be a modifiable unsigned integer lvalue (e.g., uint32_t, unsigned, size_t) with at least 32 bits.
x is modified in place and evaluated multiple times; do not pass expressions with side effects.
Behavior for x==0 underflows the pre-decrement; only use with positive values when semantics matter.
Shifts assume at least 32-bit width; on narrower types the macro is invalid/undefined.

functions.name: kvec_t
functions.signature: unknown (macro type template: kvec_t(T) expands to struct { size_t n, m; T *a; })
functions.description: Macro that expands to a simple dynamic array structure with fields n (size), m (capacity), and a (pointer to elements of type T). Used to declare vector variables, e.g., kvec_t(int) v;
requirements: Supply a concrete element type T when using kvec_t(T).
Before use, initialize the instance with kv_init(v).
Access and mutation should be done via provided macros to maintain invariants.

functions.name: kv_init
functions.description: Initializes a kvec_t(T) instance by setting size and capacity to 0 and the data pointer to NULL. Does not allocate memory.
requirements: v must be an lvalue of type kvec_t(T).
Safe to call on a zeroed or uninitialized kvec_t(T) variable; after calling, the vector is empty and has no allocation.
After kv_destroy(v), call kv_init(v) again before reuse.

functions.name: kv_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a kvec_t(T) instance by freeing its backing array pointer. Does not modify n or m.
requirements: v must be an lvalue of type kvec_t(T).
Safe to call if v.a is NULL; free(NULL) is a no-op.
Do not access v.a after destroy unless reinitialized or reassigned.
If you intend to reuse v immediately, reinitialize with kv_init(v) or reset fields appropriately.

functions.name: kv_A
functions.description: Unchecked element access macro that returns the lvalue at index i (v.a[i]). Provides static, direct access without bounds checks.
requirements: v must be a valid kvec_t(T) with a non-NULL a when n>0.
i must satisfy 0 <= i < v.n; no bounds checking is performed.
The caller must ensure that the element has been initialized before reading.

functions.name: kv_pop
functions.description: Pops and returns the last element in the vector (pre-decrements n, then returns a[n]). No bounds checks.
requirements: v must be an initialized kvec_t(T) whose n > 0 before the call.
Invoking when v.n == 0 leads to underflow/undefined behavior.
The returned value is a copy of the last element; for pointer types, no destructor is run.

functions.name: kv_size
functions.description: Returns the current number of elements (n) in the vector.
requirements: v must be a kvec_t(T).

functions.name: kv_max
functions.description: Returns the current capacity (m) of the vector (number of elements a can hold).
requirements: v must be a kvec_t(T).

functions.name: kv_resize
functions.description: Resizes the vector’s capacity to exactly s elements by setting m = s and reallocating a to sizeof(type) * m. Does not change n.
requirements: type must match the element type of v (the T in kvec_t(T)).
v must be an initialized kvec_t(T).
s is the desired capacity (size_t). If s < v.n, n is NOT adjusted; caller must ensure v.n <= s after resize to avoid out-of-bounds writes.

On allocation failure, realloc returns NULL and the old buffer is lost due to direct assignment; this results in data loss and makes v.a NULL. The macro performs no error checking; callers must be robust to this possibility if failures are possible.
If s == 0, a may become NULL and m becomes 0.

functions.name: kv_copy
functions.description: Copies the contents of v0 into v1 by ensuring v1 has capacity >= v0.n, setting v1.n = v0.n, and memcpy’ing v0.n elements of sizeof(type) from v0.a to v1.a.
requirements: type must match the element type of both vectors.
v1 and v0 must be kvec_t(T) and may be distinct vectors; their buffers must be non-overlapping for memcpy (typical use).
Relies on realloc inside kv_resize; on allocation failure for v1, v1.a may become NULL and subsequent memcpy will dereference NULL (undefined behavior). No error checking is performed.
Callers should ensure v0.a is non-NULL if v0.n > 0; memcpy with NULL source and nonzero length is undefined.
To compile, ensure memcpy is declared (typically include <string.h>).

functions.name: kv_push
functions.description: Appends element x to the end of vector v. Grows capacity by doubling (starting at 2) using realloc as needed, then assigns and increments n.
requirements: type must match the element type of v.
v must be initialized with kv_init(v).

On capacity growth, realloc may return NULL; the macro assigns directly to v.a without checking. A failure leads to v.a == NULL and the subsequent assignment will dereference NULL (undefined behavior).
x is evaluated exactly once in the assignment (no multiple evaluation in the macro body).

functions.name: kv_pushp
functions.description: Appends an uninitialized element slot and returns a pointer to it ((v).a + ((v).n++)). Grows capacity by doubling (starting at 2) using realloc if needed.
requirements: type must match the element type of v.
v must be initialized with kv_init(v).
On capacity growth, realloc may return NULL; the macro assigns directly to v.a without checking. A failure leads to returning a pointer derived from NULL (undefined behavior).
The returned pointer may be invalidated by subsequent reallocations; use it immediately or store only until next potential growth.

functions.name: kv_a
functions.description: Ensures the vector is large enough to index i, growing capacity to at least i+1 (rounded up using kv_roundup32) and setting n to i+1 if needed. Returns an lvalue reference to v.a[i] for assignment or access.
requirements: type must match the element type of v.
v must be initialized with kv_init(v).
i must be convertible to size_t and intended to be within representable bounds; negative values cast to large size_t will cause huge allocations/undefined behavior.
When i >= m, the macro sets m = n = i + 1, rounds m up via kv_roundup32, and reallocates; realloc failure is unchecked and leads to v.a == NULL and subsequent dereference (undefined behavior).
When n <= i < m, the macro updates n = i + 1 without reallocating.
Access is unchecked; caller must ensure that use of the returned lvalue is valid for T.

functions.name: kmp_init_##name
functions.description: Create and initialize a memory pool instance for elements of the pool’s node type. Returns a newly allocated, zero-initialized pool object. Intended to be called before any kmp_alloc_##name/kmp_free_##name operations.
requirements: May return NULL on allocation failure; the caller should check the return value before use.
The returned pool must be destroyed with kmp_destroy_##name when no longer needed.
This function performs dynamic allocation (calloc).

functions.name: kmp_destroy_##name
functions.description: Destroy a memory pool previously created by kmp_init_##name, freeing the pool’s internal buffer and every cached element by first calling the provided element-free function (kmpfree_f) and then free().
requirements: mp must be a valid pointer returned by kmp_init_##name.
All objects allocated from this pool should be returned via kmp_free_##name before destroying the pool to avoid leaks or dangling references.
Do not use mp after this call (the pointer becomes invalid).
Behavior is undefined if mp is NULL.

functions.name: kmp_alloc_##name
functions.description: Allocate an element from the memory pool. If the pool has cached elements, one is returned; otherwise a new zero-initialized element is allocated with calloc. Returns a pointer to the element.
requirements: mp must be a valid pointer returned by kmp_init_##name.
May return NULL if allocation fails; callers should check the result.
Elements returned from the cache are not zeroed; callers should initialize any required fields before use.
The returned element must be returned to the same pool via kmp_free_##name; do not free() it directly.
Do not use the element after returning it to the pool.

functions.name: kmp_free_##name
functions.signature: static inline klib_unused void kmp_free_##name(kmp_##name##_t *mp, kmptype_t *p)
functions.description: Return an element previously obtained from kmp_alloc_##name to the pool’s free list for reuse. May grow the pool’s internal buffer to store the returned pointer.
requirements: mp must be a valid pointer returned by kmp_init_##name.
p must be a pointer previously returned by kmp_alloc_##name from the same pool instance.
Do not pass NULL for p.
Do not double-free the same element; behavior is undefined.
After this call, p must not be dereferenced by the caller.

functions.name: kl_init_##name
functions.description: Create and initialize a singly-linked list that uses an internal memory pool for node management. Allocates the list object and an initial dummy tail node, sets head and tail to that node, and initializes size to 0.
requirements: May return NULL on allocation failure; callers should check the returned pointer before use.
Internally allocates at least one list node using the memory pool; if that allocation were to fail, subsequent use would be invalid/undefined.
The returned list must be destroyed with kl_destroy_##name when no longer needed.

functions.name: kl_destroy_##name
functions.description: Destroy a list previously created by kl_init_##name. Returns all list nodes (including the sentinel/dummy nodes) to the internal pool, destroys the pool, and frees the list structure.
requirements: kl must be a valid pointer returned by kl_init_##name.
All external references/iterators to list nodes become invalid after this call; do not dereference them.
Do not use kl after this call (the pointer becomes invalid).
Behavior is undefined if kl is NULL.

functions.name: kl_pushp_##name
functions.description: Append a new element to the end of the list and return a pointer to the data field of the newly appended node (specifically, the data slot of the former tail node). The caller should write the element’s value to the returned location.
requirements: kl must be a valid pointer returned by kl_init_##name.
May fail (returning a pointer derived from a NULL allocation) if the internal allocation fails; callers should be prepared for allocation failure in constrained environments.
The returned pointer refers to internal list storage and is valid until that node is removed (e.g., by kl_shift_##name) or the list is destroyed.
Callers should initialize/write the element value to the returned location before performing operations that may consume it (e.g., kl_shift_##name).

functions.name: kl_shift_##name
functions.signature: static inline klib_unused int kl_shift_##name(kl_##name##_t *kl, kltype_t *d)
functions.description: Remove the element at the head of the list (FIFO). If the list is non-empty, optionally store the removed element’s data to *d (if d is non-NULL), return the node to the pool, decrement size, and return 0. If the list is empty, return -1 and leave the list unchanged.
requirements: kl must be a valid pointer returned by kl_init_##name.
d may be NULL if the caller does not need the removed value.
Callers must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates the list was empty and no data was removed.
Any pointer previously returned by kl_pushp_##name for the removed node becomes invalid after this call.

functions.name: __ac_X31_hash_string
functions.description: Computes a hash value for a null-terminated C string using an X31 rolling hash. Intended for hashing const char* keys in khash tables. Call with a valid, null-terminated string pointer; does not modify input and has no side effects.
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated string
The pointed-to memory must be readable for the length of the string
Thread-safe and reentrant; no global state used

functions.name: __ac_Wang_hash
functions.description: Applies Thomas Wang’s integer hash mix to the provided key to produce a well-distributed khint_t hash value. Used internally by khash as an alternative integer hash function.
requirements: Accepts any khint_t value; no specific range constraints

functions.name: kh_init_##name
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an empty hash table instance for the instantiation identified by “name”. Usage: call after KHASH_INIT/KHASH_DECLARE has created kh_##name##_t. Returns a zero-initialized table object ready for use.
requirements: Must be used with a previously declared/instantiated hash type via KHASH_INIT/KHASH_DECLARE so that kh_##name##_t is defined.
Return value must be checked for NULL if the allocator is overridden or may fail (kcalloc).
No arguments.

functions.name: kh_destroy_##name
functions.description: Destroys a hash table instance and frees internal buffers for keys, flags, and values (if map). Safe to pass NULL; does nothing in that case.
requirements: If h is non-NULL, it must point to a kh_##name##_t created by kh_init_##name.
After calling, h becomes invalid; do not use it further.
Safe to call with h == NULL.

functions.name: kh_clear_##name
functions.description: Resets the table to empty without deallocating the key/value/flag buffers. Preserves capacity for reuse.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized kh_##name##_t pointer.
After clear, previous iterators/bucket indices are not guaranteed to remain meaningful for access (table is logically empty).

functions.name: kh_get_##name
functions.description: Looks up key and returns the bucket index if found; returns kh_end(h) if absent. Uses quadratic probing with the hash and equality functions bound in the instantiation.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
key must be of the khkey_t type used in the instantiation.
Caller must compare return value against kh_end(h) to detect absence before using the index.

functions.name: kh_resize_##name
functions.description: Rehashes the table to have at least new_n_buckets buckets (rounded up to a power of two, minimum 4). May shrink or expand and moves elements as needed. Returns 0 on success, -1 on allocation failure.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
Caller must check the return value and handle -1 (allocation failure).
Resizing may move elements; previously obtained iterators/bucket indices can be invalidated.
new_n_buckets is adjusted internally (rounded up to power of two; minimum 4).

functions.name: kh_put_##name
functions.description: Inserts key if absent, or finds the existing slot if present. On success returns the bucket index. Writes ret: -1 on failure; 0 if key already present; 1 if inserted into a never-used bucket; 2 if inserted into a previously-deleted bucket. May resize the table internally.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
key must be of the khkey_t type used in the instantiation.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the status code.
Caller must check *ret for -1 (failure) and should not modify keys when *ret == 0 (existing key).
On successful insert (ret == 1 or 2), for maps the caller can assign the value via kh_value(h, idx).
May invalidate existing iterators/bucket indices due to internal resizing.

functions.name: kh_del_##name
functions.description: Deletes the element at bucket index x, if x is valid and occupied. Marks the slot as deleted and decrements size.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
x should be a bucket index previously obtained (e.g., from kh_get/kh_put) and must not be kh_end(h).

Calling with an invalid x or an empty/deleted bucket has no effect on occupied entries per implementation guard; callers should ensure x refers to an existing element (kh_exist(h,x) != 0) before deleting.

functions.name: kh_init
functions.description: Macro wrapper: expands to kh_init_##name(). Creates a new table instance for the given instantiation name. Usage: khash_t(name)* h = kh_init(name);
requirements: name must be an instantiated khash type identifier as used with KHASH_INIT/KHASH_DECLARE.
Result should be checked for NULL if allocation can fail.

functions.name: kh_destroy
functions.description: Macro wrapper: expands to kh_destroy_##name(h). Destroys the table and frees its resources.
requirements: name must match the instantiation of h.
h may be NULL; otherwise must point to a valid table.

functions.name: kh_clear
functions.description: Macro wrapper: expands to kh_clear_##name(h). Clears contents without freeing capacity.
requirements: name must match the instantiation of h.
h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.

functions.name: kh_resize
functions.description: Macro wrapper: expands to kh_resize_##name(h, s). Rehashes the table to have approximately s buckets (rounded up internally). Returns int (0 on success, -1 on failure).
requirements: name must match the instantiation of h.
h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
Caller must check the return value and handle -1.
Resizing may invalidate iterators/bucket indices.

functions.name: kh_put
functions.description: Macro wrapper: expands to kh_put_##name(h, k, r). Inserts key k and returns bucket index; writes status to *r (-1 failure, 0 present, 1 empty, 2 deleted).
requirements: name must match the instantiation of h.
h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
r must be a non-NULL int* for the status code.
Caller must check *r for -1 and for presence vs insertion before using kh_value on maps.

functions.name: kh_get
functions.description: Macro wrapper: expands to kh_get_##name(h, k). Looks up k and returns bucket index or kh_end(h) if absent.
requirements: name must match the instantiation of h.
h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
Caller must compare returned index against kh_end(h) before access.

functions.name: kh_del
functions.description: Macro wrapper: expands to kh_del_##name(h, k). Deletes element at bucket index k (iterator).
requirements: name must match the instantiation of h.
h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
k must be a valid iterator index where kh_exist(h,k) is true; must not be kh_end(h).

functions.name: kh_exist
functions.description: Macro: returns 1 if bucket x contains data; 0 otherwise. Implemented as !__ac_iseither((h)->flags, (x)).
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer of a matching instantiation.
x must be a bucket index in the range [kh_begin(h), kh_end(h)).

functions.name: kh_key
functions.description: Macro: returns the key stored at bucket index x: (h)->keys[x].
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
x must be a valid, occupied bucket index (kh_exist(h,x) must be nonzero).
Only use when the table is instantiated with a key type khkey_t matching the instantiation.

functions.name: kh_val
functions.description: Macro: returns the value at bucket index x: (h)->vals[x]. Note: for hash sets, calling this results in a segfault (no vals array).
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer instantiated as a map (with kh_is_map = 1).
x must be a valid, occupied bucket index (kh_exist(h,x) must be nonzero).
Do not use on hash sets (KHASH_SET_*); it will segfault.

functions.name: kh_value
functions.description: Macro alias of kh_val(h, x). Returns the value at bucket index x for maps.
requirements: Same as kh_val: only for map instantiations; h must be valid; x must be an occupied bucket index.

functions.name: kh_begin
functions.description: Macro: returns the starting iterator index for traversal, always 0.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
Use with kh_end(h) and kh_exist(h, i) when iterating.

functions.name: kh_end
functions.description: Macro: returns the end-iterator index: (h)->n_buckets. Used as a sentinel; no element resides at this index.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.
Do not use the returned index to access keys/values; compare against it to detect absence.

functions.name: kh_size
functions.description: Macro: returns the number of elements currently stored: (h)->size.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.

functions.name: kh_n_buckets
functions.description: Macro: returns the total number of buckets allocated: (h)->n_buckets.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer.

functions.name: kh_foreach
functions.description: Macro to iterate over all occupied entries. Expands to a for loop from kh_begin(h) to kh_end(h), skipping empty/deleted buckets, assigning key to kvar and value to vvar, then executing code.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer instantiated as a map (uses kh_val).
kvar must be a variable of the key type; vvar must be a variable of the value type.
Within the loop, ensure kh_val is valid for the instantiation (do not use with sets).

functions.name: kh_foreach_value
functions.description: Macro to iterate over all occupied values. Expands to a for loop assigning each value to vvar and executing code.
requirements: h must be a valid, initialized table pointer instantiated as a map (uses kh_val).
vvar must be a variable of the value type.
Do not use with sets; kh_val is invalid for sets.

functions.name: kavl_find_suf
functions.signature: T* kavl_find_suf(const T* root, const T* x, unsigned* cnt_)
functions.description: Locate a node equal to x in the AVL tree defined via KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suffix "suf". Uses the user-supplied comparator to traverse from root; if found, returns the matching node pointer; otherwise returns NULL. If cnt_ is non-NULL, it is set to the number of nodes <= x (rank). Intended for read-only lookup using a key-like temporary T with key fields set.
requirements: Must be generated by invoking KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suf == "suf" on type T and comparator cmp.
root may be NULL (empty tree).
x must be a valid pointer to a T whose key fields (read by the comparator) are initialized; x does not need to be a node already in the tree.
If cnt_ is non-NULL, it will be written with the rank (number of nodes smaller than or equal to x).
The comparator provided in KAVL_INIT defines ordering and equality.

functions.name: kavl_interval_suf
functions.signature: T* kavl_interval_suf(const T* root, const T* x, T** lower, T** upper)
functions.description: Find the node equal to x if present; additionally compute in-order neighbors around x. Sets *lower to the greatest node < x and *upper to the smallest node > x (or both to the found node if equal). Returns the node equal to x when present, otherwise NULL. Either lower or upper may be NULL to skip that output.
requirements: Must be generated by KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suf == "suf" on type T and comparator cmp.
root may be NULL (empty tree).
x must be a valid pointer to a T whose key fields used by the comparator are initialized; it need not be in the tree.
lower and/or upper may be NULL; non-NULL pointers will be written with neighbor results (or NULL if none).
Uses the comparator to determine ordering and equality.

functions.name: kavl_insert_suf
functions.signature: T* kavl_insert_suf(T** root_, T* x, unsigned* cnt_)
functions.description: Insert node x into the AVL tree rooted at *root_. If an equal key already exists, does not insert and returns the existing node; otherwise links x and rebalances as needed, possibly updating *root_. If cnt_ is non-NULL, it is set to the number of nodes <= x at the time of insertion/search (rank).
requirements: Must be generated by KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suf == "suf" on type T and comparator cmp.
root_ must be a valid pointer to the tree root; *root_ may be NULL (empty tree) or a valid tree built with the same KAVL setup.
x must be a valid, heap- (or otherwise) allocated T with its comparator-consumed key fields initialized.
x must contain the KAVL_HEAD member specified in KAVL_INIT; its linkage fields will be written by this function and must not be pre-linked into another tree.
If an equal node is already present, that existing node is returned and x is left untouched (caller typically frees x if it was newly allocated).
If cnt_ is non-NULL, it will be written with the rank (number of nodes smaller than or equal to x).
No user comparator side effects that invalidate tree invariants.

functions.name: kavl_erase_suf
functions.signature: T* kavl_erase_suf(T** root_, const T* x, unsigned* cnt_)
functions.description: Remove a node from the AVL tree. If x is non-NULL, it is treated as a key: the function searches for a node equal to x (by comparator) and removes it. If x is NULL, removes the first (smallest) node. Returns the removed node on success, or NULL if no matching node exists. Rebalances and may update *root_. If cnt_ is non-NULL and x is non-NULL, it is set to the number of nodes <= x at search time.
requirements: Must be generated by KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suf == "suf" on type T and comparator cmp.
root_ must be a valid pointer to the tree root; *root_ may be NULL (empty tree) or a valid tree built with the same KAVL setup.
If x is non-NULL, it must be a valid pointer to a T whose key fields used by the comparator are initialized; it need not be the same address as the stored node.
If x is NULL, the smallest element (in-order first) is removed.
On success the returned node is unlinked and owned by the caller (caller is responsible for freeing it if dynamically allocated).
If cnt_ is non-NULL and x is non-NULL, it will be written with the rank (number of nodes smaller than or equal to x).

functions.name: kavl_itr_first_suf
functions.signature: void kavl_itr_first_suf(const T* root, struct kavl_itr_suf* itr)
functions.description: Initialize an in-order iterator at the smallest element in the tree. Populates itr to point at the leftmost node, or to an empty state if root is NULL. Subsequent iteration uses kavl_itr_next_bidir_suf with dir=1 for forward or dir=0 for backward traversal.
requirements: Must be generated by KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suf == "suf" so that struct kavl_itr_suf is defined for T.
root may be NULL (empty tree).
itr must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct kavl_itr_suf instance; its internal stack is overwritten.
Tree must not be mutated in ways that invalidate node addresses while iterating unless the iterator is reinitialized afterward.

functions.name: kavl_itr_find_suf
functions.signature: int kavl_itr_find_suf(const T* root, const T* x, struct kavl_itr_suf* itr)
functions.description: Position an iterator to the node equal to x if present; otherwise to the in-order predecessor/successor boundary so that a following forward step yields the first node > x. Returns 1 if a node equal to x was found, 0 otherwise. After a 0 return, kavl_at(itr) is NULL iff x is larger than all nodes.
requirements: Must be generated by KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suf == "suf" so that struct kavl_itr_suf is defined for T and comparator is available.
root may be NULL (empty tree).
x must be a valid pointer to a T with comparator-visible key fields initialized; it need not be in the tree.
itr must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a struct kavl_itr_suf; it is reinitialized by this call.
Interpret return value: 1 means exact match at iterator; 0 means not found; use kavl_at(itr) to inspect current pointer (may be NULL if x is greater than all nodes).

functions.name: kavl_itr_next_bidir_suf
functions.signature: int kavl_itr_next_bidir_suf(struct kavl_itr_suf* itr, int dir)
functions.description: Advance a bidirectional iterator by one step. If dir!=0, moves forward to the next in-order node; if dir==0, moves backward to the previous node. Returns 1 if movement succeeded (iterator now points to a valid node), or 0 if there is no next/previous element (iterator becomes empty when stepping past ends).
requirements: Must be generated by KAVL_INIT/KAVL_INIT2 with suf == "suf" so that struct kavl_itr_suf is defined for T.
itr must be a valid, initialized iterator produced by kavl_itr_first_suf or kavl_itr_find_suf (or a prior successful step).
dir is treated as boolean: 1 for next, 0 for previous.
Do not modify the underlying tree structure while iterating unless you reinitialize or reposition the iterator, as structural changes can invalidate the iterator state.

functions.name: kavl_insert
functions.description: Macro wrapper that inserts node x into an AVL tree instantiated by KAVL_INIT. Expands to kavl_insert_##suf(proot, x, cnt). Returns x if it was inserted, or the equal existing node if a duplicate was found. cnt, if non-NULL, receives the number of nodes smaller than or equal to x.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked with matching suf, type, head field, and comparator in the same translation unit.
proot must be a valid pointer to the root pointer (it may point to a NULL root initially).
x must be a valid pointer to a node of type __type that contains the __head member as declared by KAVL_HEAD.
cnt may be NULL; if non-NULL it points to an unsigned to receive the rank.
If an equal node already exists, the tree is not modified and that existing node is returned; callers should not insert x in that case (example shows freeing x).

functions.name: kavl_find
functions.description: Macro wrapper that looks up x in the AVL tree. Expands to kavl_find_##suf(root, x, cnt). Returns the equal node if present, or NULL if absent. cnt, if non-NULL, receives the number of nodes smaller than or equal to x.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked with matching parameters.
root may be NULL (empty tree) or point to a valid tree root.
x must point to a probe value/node compatible with the comparator __cmp used at instantiation.
cnt may be NULL; if non-NULL it points to an unsigned to receive the rank.

functions.name: kavl_interval
functions.description: Macro wrapper that searches for x and also reports neighbors. Expands to kavl_interval_##suf(root, x, lower, upper). Returns the equal node if present, otherwise NULL. If not found, lower receives the greatest node less than x and upper the least node greater than x (either output may be NULL).
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked with matching parameters.
root may be NULL (empty tree) or a valid tree root.
x must be a probe value/node compatible with the comparator.
lower and/or upper may be NULL; non-NULL pointers must be valid to receive outputs.

functions.name: kavl_erase
functions.description: Macro wrapper that removes a node equal to x from the AVL tree. Expands to kavl_erase_##suf(proot, x, cnt). Returns the removed node if present, or NULL if absent. If cnt is non-NULL, it receives the number of nodes smaller than or equal to x.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked with matching parameters.
proot must be a valid pointer to the root pointer of a tree possibly modified in-place.
x may be NULL only when used via kavl_erase_first; otherwise it points to a probe value/node used for comparison.
cnt may be NULL; if non-NULL it points to an unsigned to receive the rank.
The returned node (if non-NULL) is detached from the tree; caller is responsible for any deallocation if needed.

functions.name: kavl_erase_first
functions.signature: __type* kavl_erase_##suf(__type **proot, const __type *x, unsigned *cnt)  // macro uses x=NULL, cnt=NULL
functions.description: Macro wrapper that removes and returns the smallest node in the tree. It expands to kavl_erase_##suf(proot, 0, 0). Returns the removed node, or NULL if the tree is empty.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked with matching parameters.
proot must be a valid pointer to the root pointer; the root may change.
Caller is responsible for any deallocation of the returned node.

functions.name: kavl_itr_first
functions.description: Macro wrapper that positions an iterator at the smallest element. Expands to kavl_itr_first_##suf(root, itr). After this call, kavl_at(itr) returns the smallest node or NULL if the tree is empty.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked so that struct kavl_itr_##suf is defined.
root may be NULL (empty tree) or a valid tree root.
itr must be a valid pointer to an iterator object of type struct kavl_itr_##suf.

functions.name: kavl_itr_find
functions.description: Macro wrapper that positions an iterator at the node equal to x if present, or at the in-order predecessor/successor path for further navigation. Expands to kavl_itr_find_##suf(root, x, itr). Returns 1 if an equal node was found, 0 otherwise. Per the header comment, kavl_at(itr) is NULL if and only if the query is larger than all objects in the tree.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked so that struct kavl_itr_##suf is defined.
root may be NULL (empty tree) or a valid tree root.
x must be a probe value/node compatible with the comparator.
itr must be a valid pointer to an iterator object of type struct kavl_itr_##suf.

functions.name: kavl_itr_next
functions.signature: int kavl_itr_next_bidir_##suf(struct kavl_itr_##suf *itr, int dir)  // macro uses dir=1
functions.description: Macro wrapper that advances the iterator to the next in-order element. Expands to kavl_itr_next_bidir_##suf(itr, 1). Returns 1 if there is a next object; 0 otherwise.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked so that struct kavl_itr_##suf is defined.
itr must be a valid pointer to an initialized iterator (e.g., via kavl_itr_first or kavl_itr_find).

functions.name: kavl_itr_prev
functions.signature: int kavl_itr_next_bidir_##suf(struct kavl_itr_##suf *itr, int dir)  // macro uses dir=0
functions.description: Macro wrapper that moves the iterator to the previous in-order element. Expands to kavl_itr_next_bidir_##suf(itr, 0). Returns 1 if there is a previous object; 0 otherwise.
requirements: KAVL_INIT(suf, __type, __head, __cmp) must have been invoked so that struct kavl_itr_##suf is defined.
itr must be a valid pointer to an initialized iterator (e.g., via kavl_itr_first or kavl_itr_find).

functions.name: kavl_at
functions.signature: const __type* kavl_at(const struct kavl_itr_##suf *itr)  // macro yields ((itr)->top < (itr)->stack ? NULL : *(itr)->top)
functions.description: Macro that returns the node pointer at the iterator’s current position, or NULL if the iterator is before the first element or the tree is empty. After kavl_itr_find, it is NULL iff the query is larger than all elements.
requirements: itr must be a valid pointer to a struct kavl_itr_##suf previously positioned with an iterator function.

functions.name: kavll_at
functions.description: Returns the current node pointed to by an in-order iterator produced by the KAVLL iterator API. This is a macro, not a real function; it dereferences the iterator’s internal stack/top to yield the current element, or returns NULL when the iterator is before the first element or has been exhausted. Typical usage: initialize or position an iterator with pre_itr_first(), pre_itr_find(), and advance with pre_itr_next(); then call kavll_at(&itr) to obtain the current node.
requirements: itr must be a valid, non-null pointer to a pre##_itr_t produced by __KAVLL_ITR (via KAVLL_INIT/KAVLL_INIT2).

itr must have been initialized/positioned by pre##_itr_first(root, &itr) or pre##_itr_find(root, x, &itr), and optionally advanced by pre##_itr_next(&itr) before calling kavll_at; otherwise it may return NULL.
The returned pointer type is const __type*; do not modify the node through this pointer unless your node definition and usage permit casting away const (not recommended).
kavll_at returns NULL when (itr->top < itr->stack), which indicates the iterator is not positioned on a valid element (e.g., iteration completed or not yet initialized).
Caller must treat a NULL return as "no current element" and avoid dereferencing it.

functions.name: kdq_init_##type
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new deque instance for the given element type. Starts with capacity 1<<2 and zero elements. Use when you need a type-specialized deque before pushing or shifting elements. Returns a pointer to the newly allocated queue object.
requirements: The template parameter 'type' must be a valid C type token used consistently with KDQ_INIT/KDQ_DECLARE.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL if allocation can fail in the target environment.
The returned deque must later be destroyed with kdq_destroy_##type to avoid memory leaks.
Do not use the deque before successful initialization.

functions.name: kdq_destroy_##type
functions.description: Destroys a deque instance and frees its internal buffer. Safe to call with NULL. Use when finished with the deque to release resources.
requirements: If q is non-NULL, it must point to a deque previously initialized by kdq_init_##type (or KDQ_INIT-generated inline version).
After calling, the pointer q becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: kdq_resize_##type
functions.description: Resizes the deque’s underlying circular buffer to a capacity of 1<<new_bits (or larger if needed to fit existing elements). Preserves element order while handling wrapped/unwrapped layouts. Returns the resulting bits value (log2 of capacity). Typically used internally on push/unshift, but can be called to reserve/shrink storage.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized deque pointer.
new_bits should be >= 0; capacity is computed as 1ULL<<new_bits.
If new_bits is too small for the current count, the function will increase it to the minimum that fits the elements.
Pointers into the internal array (from previous pushp/unshiftp/pop/shift) may be invalidated by this call due to reallocation.
Caller should handle potential allocation failures according to the environment; the code does not explicitly report realloc/malloc failures beyond returning the (possibly unchanged) bits.

functions.name: kdq_pushp_##type
functions.description: Appends a new uninitialized element slot at the back of the deque and returns a pointer to it. The caller should write the element value through the returned pointer. Automatically grows capacity as needed.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized deque pointer.
The returned pointer points into the deque’s internal buffer and may be invalidated by subsequent operations that reallocate or move storage (e.g., push/unshift/resize).
Caller must initialize the returned slot before using the element.
May trigger a resize; ensure the environment can handle allocations.

functions.name: kdq_push_##type
functions.description: Appends a copy of v to the back of the deque, growing capacity as needed. Use to enqueue elements at the tail.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized deque pointer.
v must be a valid instance of 'type' suitable for copying/assignment into the internal buffer.
May trigger a resize; ensure the environment can handle allocations.

functions.name: kdq_unshiftp_##type
functions.description: Prepends a new uninitialized element slot at the front of the deque and returns a pointer to it. The caller should write the element value through the returned pointer. Automatically grows capacity as needed.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized deque pointer.
The returned pointer points into the deque’s internal buffer and may be invalidated by subsequent operations that reallocate or move storage (e.g., push/unshift/resize).
Caller must initialize the returned slot before using the element.
May trigger a resize; ensure the environment can handle allocations.

functions.name: kdq_unshift_##type
functions.description: Prepends a copy of v to the front of the deque, growing capacity as needed. Use to enqueue elements at the head.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized deque pointer.
v must be a valid instance of 'type' suitable for copying/assignment into the internal buffer.
May trigger a resize; ensure the environment can handle allocations.

functions.name: kdq_pop_##type
functions.description: Removes the element at the back of the deque and returns a pointer to the removed element within the internal buffer, or NULL if the deque is empty. Useful for stack-like pop from the tail.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized deque pointer.
If the deque is empty, the function returns NULL; callers must check for NULL before dereferencing.
The returned pointer points into internal storage and may be invalidated by subsequent operations that modify or resize the deque.

functions.name: kdq_shift_##type
functions.description: Removes the element at the front of the deque and returns a pointer to the removed element within the internal buffer, or NULL if the deque is empty. Useful for queue-like dequeue from the head.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized deque pointer.
If the deque is empty, the function returns NULL; callers must check for NULL before dereferencing.
The returned pointer points into internal storage and may be invalidated by subsequent operations that modify or resize the deque.

functions.name: kdq_init
functions.signature: For element type T: kdq_T_t* kdq_init_T(void)  [Accessed via macro kdq_init(T)]
functions.description: Initializes a new double-ended queue (ring buffer) for elements of type T and returns a heap-allocated kdq_T_t*. This is a macro wrapper; you must first declare/define the type-specific API using KDQ_DECLARE(T) and KDQ_INIT2(T, SCOPE) or KDQ_INIT(T). Use when you need an empty deque with initial capacity 2^2.
requirements: Caller must have instantiated the type-specific deque with KDQ_INIT(T) (or declared with KDQ_DECLARE(T) and defined with KDQ_INIT2).
Returns a non-null pointer on success; allocation can fail (calloc/malloc). Caller must check for NULL before use.
Resulting queue must be freed with kdq_destroy(T, q).

functions.name: kdq_destroy
functions.signature: For element type T: void kdq_destroy_T(kdq_T_t* q)  [Accessed via macro kdq_destroy(T, q)]
functions.description: Destroys a type-specific deque instance, freeing its internal array and the deque object. Safe to call with NULL (no-op). Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a kdq_T_t* previously returned by kdq_init_T (or compatible) or NULL.
After return, q and its internal buffer must not be used.

functions.name: kdq_resize
functions.signature: For element type T: int kdq_resize_T(kdq_T_t* q, int new_bits)  [Accessed via macro kdq_resize(T, q, new_bits)]
functions.description: Resizes the deque’s underlying circular buffer to a capacity of 2^new_bits elements. May grow or shrink; preserves existing elements order. Returns the resulting bits (may differ from requested if too small). Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized kdq_T_t*.
new_bits determines capacity as 2^new_bits; must be in the range [0, 63] to avoid undefined shifts and to fit the 6-bit bits field.
If requested capacity is smaller than the current element count, the function increases new_bits to the minimum that can hold all elements; the return value reflects the actual bits used.
On growth, reallocation occurs before data movement; on shrink, data may be memmoved and the internal pointer reallocated after updating metadata.
On allocation failure via realloc/malloc (not explicitly checked in code), behavior is undefined; callers should avoid forcing resize in extremely low-memory situations.

functions.name: kdq_pushp
functions.signature: For element type T: T* kdq_pushp_T(kdq_T_t* q)  [Accessed via macro kdq_pushp(T, q)]
functions.description: Appends one uninitialized element slot at the back and returns a pointer to it. Automatically grows the buffer if full. Caller writes the value into the returned slot. Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized kdq_T_t*.
Caller must write a valid T value to the returned pointer before using it via other operations.
May reallocate the internal array; previously saved element pointers become invalid after this call if a resize occurred.
If q is at capacity, it resizes by doubling (bits+1).

functions.name: kdq_push
functions.signature: For element type T: void kdq_push_T(kdq_T_t* q, T v)  [Accessed via macro kdq_push(T, q, v)]
functions.description: Appends value v to the back of the deque, resizing if necessary. Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized kdq_T_t*.
v must be a valid object of type T (copied by value into the buffer).
May trigger resize which can invalidate prior raw pointers into the internal array.

functions.name: kdq_pop
functions.signature: For element type T: T* kdq_pop_T(kdq_T_t* q)  [Accessed via macro kdq_pop(T, q)]
functions.description: Removes and returns a pointer to the last element (back) of the deque, or NULL if empty. Returned pointer refers to internal storage valid until the next modifying operation that may resize or overwrite it. Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized kdq_T_t*.
If the deque is empty, returns NULL; caller must check for NULL before dereferencing.
Returned pointer becomes invalid after any operation that resizes or overwrites that slot.

functions.name: kdq_unshiftp
functions.signature: For element type T: T* kdq_unshiftp_T(kdq_T_t* q)  [Accessed via macro kdq_unshiftp(T, q)]
functions.description: Prepends one uninitialized element slot at the front and returns a pointer to it. Automatically grows the buffer if full. Caller writes the value into the returned slot. Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized kdq_T_t*.
Caller must write a valid T value to the returned pointer before using it via other operations.
May reallocate the internal array; any previously obtained raw element pointers can be invalidated.
If q is at capacity, it resizes by doubling (bits+1).

functions.name: kdq_unshift
functions.signature: For element type T: void kdq_unshift_T(kdq_T_t* q, T v)  [Accessed via macro kdq_unshift(T, q, v)]
functions.description: Prepends value v to the front of the deque, resizing if necessary. Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized kdq_T_t*.
v must be a valid object of type T (copied by value).
May trigger resize which can invalidate prior raw pointers into the internal array.

functions.name: kdq_shift
functions.signature: For element type T: T* kdq_shift_T(kdq_T_t* q)  [Accessed via macro kdq_shift(T, q)]
functions.description: Removes and returns a pointer to the first element (front) of the deque, or NULL if empty. Returned pointer refers to internal storage valid until the next modifying operation that may resize or overwrite it. Macro wrapper over the type-specific function.
requirements: q must be a valid, initialized kdq_T_t*.
If the deque is empty, returns NULL; caller must check for NULL before dereferencing.
Returned pointer becomes invalid after any operation that resizes or overwrites that slot.

functions.name: kbi_popcount64
functions.description: Counts the number of set bits (population count) in a 64-bit unsigned integer using a branchless bit-hack implementation. Typical usage: pass any uint64_t value and receive a value in [0,64]. Pure, no side effects.
requirements: Argument y must be a 64-bit unsigned integer (uint64_t).
Return value ranges from 0 to 64 inclusive.
No special initialization or state is required; function is pure and thread-safe.

functions.name: kbi_DNAcount64
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t kbi_DNAcount64(uint64_t y, int c)
functions.description: Counts the number of occurrences of a nucleotide, encoded in 2-bit format, within a 64-bit word. The word y is assumed to hold 2-bit packed bases (up to 32 bases). The parameter c selects which base to count via its 2-bit code (as used by BWA); the exact A/C/G/T↔code mapping is not specified here. Returns the count of bases equal to c.
requirements: Argument y must contain DNA bases packed as 2-bit codes across the 64-bit word (i.e., up to 32 bases).
Argument c must be the 2-bit code (0..3) for the base to count in the same encoding used to produce y; the exact mapping to A/C/G/T is not specified here.
Return value ranges from 0 to 32 inclusive (since 64 bits hold 32 two-bit symbols).
Function is pure and thread-safe; no external state is accessed.

functions.name: kroundup32
functions.description: Rounds an integer variable up to the next power of two using a sequence of bitwise operations (classic "bit twiddling hacks" pattern). This macro modifies its argument in place and evaluates it multiple times; it is intended for an lvalue integer variable of at least 32 bits, preferably an unsigned type.
requirements: x must be a modifiable lvalue (a variable), not an expression; it is decremented and incremented inside the macro and evaluated multiple times.
x should be an unsigned integer type with width >= 32 bits to avoid undefined behavior from signed overflow and to ensure the 32-bit-wide bit spreading operates correctly.
If x is 0 (unsigned), the result will be 0 due to wraparound; for nonzero x, the result becomes the least power of two >= original x.
Do not pass arguments with side effects (e.g., x++) because the macro evaluates x multiple times.
Behavior is only defined for integer types supporting >>, |=, --, and ++; floating-point or pointer types are invalid.

functions.name: kbi_swap
functions.description: Swaps two integer variables in place using the XOR-swap trick, without a temporary. Implemented as a macro that evaluates its operands multiple times and modifies them in place.
requirements: a and b must be modifiable lvalues (variables), not expressions; each is assigned to multiple times.
a and b must refer to distinct objects; if a and b alias the same object, the value will become 0 (XOR-swap degeneracy).
a and b should have the same integral type and width to avoid unintended integer promotions or truncation during ^= and assignment.
Operands must be of integral type supporting bitwise XOR (^); pointers or floating-point types are invalid.
Do not pass arguments with side effects (e.g., a[i++]) because the macro evaluates each operand three times.

functions.name: ks_init
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a buffered byte stream (kstream_t) bound to an underlying input handle f. The stream maintains an internal buffer and read position and will be used by other ks_* functions to read bytes or delimited fields. Availability: this function is generated by KSTREAM_INIT(type_t, __read, __bufsize) and therefore depends on you instantiating that macro for your handle type and read routine.
requirements: Must be used only after KSTREAM_INIT(type_t, __read, __bufsize) has been invoked in the same translation unit to define kstream_t and ks_init.
Argument f is an initialized/valid handle of type type_t understood by the __read callback supplied to KSTREAM_INIT.
Returned kstream_t* must be destroyed with ks_destroy to free resources.
The underlying __read callback must obey: __read(f, buf, bufsize) returns number of bytes read (>0), 0 on EOF, and -1 on error.

functions.name: ks_destroy
functions.description: Free a kstream_t and its internal buffer allocated by ks_init. Safe to call with NULL; in that case it is a no-op. Availability: generated by KSTREAM_INIT(type_t, __read, __bufsize).
requirements: ks must have been created by a matching ks_init from the same KSTREAM_INIT instantiation.
May be called with ks == NULL (no effect).
After calling ks_destroy, ks must not be used.

functions.name: ks_getc
functions.description: Get the next byte from the buffered stream as an unsigned char promoted to int. Refills the internal buffer using the user-provided __read when empty. Returns -1 on EOF and -3 on underlying read error. Availability: generated by KSTREAM_INIT(type_t, __read, __bufsize).
requirements: ks must be a non-NULL pointer to a kstream_t created by ks_init.
ks must be associated with a valid underlying handle; the __read callback must be callable.
Caller must handle return values: >=0 is a byte, -1 indicates end-of-file, -3 indicates a stream/read error (ks_err(ks) becomes true).
Do not call after ks_destroy.

functions.name: ks_getuntil2
functions.signature: static int ks_getuntil2(kstream_t *ks, int delimiter, kstring_t *str, int *dret, int append)
functions.description: Read from the stream into str until a delimiter is encountered or EOF. Supports several delimiter modes: KS_SEP_LINE for line breaks (handles "\n" and trims trailing "\r"), KS_SEP_SPACE for any isspace(), KS_SEP_TAB for isspace() except space, or a specific byte value (> KS_SEP_MAX). Appends to str if append != 0; otherwise resets str length. On success, str->s is NUL-terminated and str->l is updated. If dret is non-NULL and a delimiter was found, *dret is set to the delimiter byte. Returns number of bytes stored (>=0), -1 on EOF with no data read, or -3 on stream error. Automatically grows str as needed.
requirements: ks must be a valid kstream_t created by ks_init and not yet destroyed.
str must be a valid kstring_t; its fields may be zero-initialized. The function will allocate/realloc str->s as needed and maintain NUL-termination.
delimiter must be one of: KS_SEP_SPACE, KS_SEP_TAB, KS_SEP_LINE, or a positive byte value (> KS_SEP_MAX) to match literally.
dret may be NULL; if non-NULL and a delimiter is encountered, *dret receives that delimiter byte.
append controls whether data is appended (non-zero) or str is reset (zero) before reading.
Caller must handle return values: >=0 length read; -1 indicates EOF with no data; -3 indicates a stream/read error.
If delimiter == KS_SEP_LINE and the resulting line ends with '\r', the trailing '\r' is removed.

functions.name: ks_getuntil
functions.signature: static inline int ks_getuntil(kstream_t *ks, int delimiter, kstring_t *str, int *dret)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around ks_getuntil2 with append = 0. Reads from ks into str until the specified delimiter condition is met, sets *dret to the delimiter byte if provided, NUL-terminates the string, and returns the number of bytes read, -1 on EOF with no data, or -3 on error.
requirements: Same requirements as ks_getuntil2 except append is always 0 (the current contents of str are cleared before reading).
Caller must handle return codes: >=0 length, -1 EOF with no data, -3 stream error.

functions.name: kseq_init
functions.description: Create and initialize a FASTA/FASTQ parser (kseq_t) over an input handle fd. Internally allocates a kstream_t for buffered I/O and prepares internal kstring_t fields for name, comment, sequence, and quality. Availability: defined when you instantiate KSEQ_INIT2(SCOPE, type_t, __read) (or KSEQ_INIT).
requirements: Must be used only after KSEQ_INIT2(SCOPE, type_t, __read) or KSEQ_INIT(type_t, __read) has been invoked to define kseq_t and the functions for your type_t and read routine.
fd must be a valid/initialized handle of type type_t compatible with the provided __read callback.
Returned kseq_t* must be destroyed with kseq_destroy.
Not thread-safe across shared underlying handles unless external synchronization is used (not specified here).

functions.name: kseq_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a kseq_t created by kseq_init, freeing all dynamically allocated strings (name, comment, seq, qual) and the internal kstream_t. Safe to call with NULL; it then does nothing. Availability: defined by KSEQ_INIT2/KSEQ_INIT.
requirements: ks must have been created by the matching kseq_init for the same KSEQ_INIT2/KSEQ_INIT instantiation.
May be called with ks == NULL (no effect).
After kseq_destroy returns, ks and any pointers within must not be used.

functions.name: kseq_read
functions.description: Parse and read the next FASTA or FASTQ record from the stream. Populates seq->name, seq->comment (if present), seq->seq, and for FASTQ also seq->qual. Returns the sequence length on success, -1 on end-of-file, -2 on malformed/truncated quality string, or -3 on underlying stream error. Reuses and grows internal buffers as needed; strings are NUL-terminated. On returning a FASTA record, seq->qual is left empty.
requirements: seq must be a non-NULL pointer to a kseq_t created by kseq_init and not yet destroyed.
The underlying stream must contain data in FASTA or FASTQ format; the function expects headers starting with '>' (FASTA) or '@' (FASTQ).
Caller must handle return values: >=0 sequence length on success; -1 end-of-file; -2 truncated/mismatched quality string; -3 stream/read error.
Do not modify seq->f or its internal state except via provided APIs; kseq_read manages seq->last_char and internal buffers.
kseq_rewind or kseq_rewind(ks) macro can reset the stream state if needed; otherwise records are read sequentially.

functions.name: kvsprintf
functions.signature: int kvsprintf(kstring_t *s, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-style formatting and a va_list, writing the result into the provided kstring_t buffer. Based on library conventions in this header, the formatted text is expected to be appended to s. Returns an int (likely number of characters written) but exact return semantics are not documented here.
requirements: s must point to a valid kstring_t; it should be initialized (e.g., {0,0,NULL}) so it can be grown as needed.
fmt must be a valid NUL-terminated format string compatible with printf.
ap must be an initialized va_list corresponding to fmt’s format specifiers.
Caller should handle potential failure indicated by a negative/EOF-like return if allocation fails (exact error signaling is not specified).
Resulting buffer may be reallocated; any previous s->s pointer value should not be relied on after the call.

functions.name: ksprintf
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-style formatting and writes it into the provided kstring_t buffer. By convention with other kstring functions, the result is expected to be appended to s. Returns an int (likely number of characters written) but exact return semantics are not documented here.
requirements: s must point to a valid, initialized kstring_t.
fmt must be a valid NUL-terminated printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.
Caller should check the return value for allocation/formatting failure (exact error signaling is not specified).
The underlying buffer may be reallocated; prior s->s pointer must not be used after the call without refreshing from s.

functions.name: ksplit_core
functions.signature: int ksplit_core(char *s, int delimiter, int *_max, int **_offsets);
functions.description: Core splitter that tokenizes the buffer s in-place by a single-byte delimiter, producing an array of token start offsets in _offsets and returning the number of tokens. Intended to be used via the ksplit helper, which sets up and returns the offsets array.
requirements: s must be a valid, writable, NUL-terminated string; the function may modify s (typical split implementations insert NULs).
delimiter is an int representing a single-byte delimiter; must be in the range 0..255 for byte-wise comparison.
_max must be a valid pointer to an int used internally to track capacity of *_offsets; its input value may be 0.

_offsets must be a valid pointer to an int*; on return, *_offsets points to a heap-allocated array of offsets; the caller is responsible for freeing it when no longer needed (inferred from allocation pattern).
Returns the number of tokens; on failure, likely returns 0 or a negative value, but exact failure signaling is not documented.

functions.name: kstrstr
functions.description: Substring search that finds the first occurrence of pat in str, similar to strstr. The _prep parameter appears to be an optional preprocessed table cache for the pattern to speed repeated searches.
requirements: str must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
pat must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
_prep may be NULL or point to a cache object used by the implementation; ownership/lifetime of any allocated preprocessing data is not documented here (unknown).
Returns a pointer into str to the first match or NULL if not found; caller must not free the returned pointer.

functions.name: kstrnstr
functions.signature: char *kstrnstr(const char *str, const char *pat, int n, int **_prep);
functions.description: Bounded substring search that finds the first occurrence of pat within the first n bytes of str, analogous to GNU strnstr. The _prep parameter appears to be an optional preprocessed table cache for the pattern.
requirements: str must point to a buffer of at least n bytes; if shorter and not NUL-terminated within n, behavior depends on implementation (unknown).
pat must be a valid NUL-terminated pattern string.
n must be non-negative; it limits the search extent within str.
_prep may be NULL or point to a preprocessing cache; ownership/lifetime is not documented here (unknown).
Returns a pointer into str within the first n bytes or NULL if not found; returned pointer must not be freed.

functions.name: kmemmem
functions.signature: void *kmemmem(const void *_str, int n, const void *_pat, int m, int **_prep);
functions.description: Memory search that finds the first occurrence of a byte sequence pat (length m) within a memory block str (length n), similar to GNU memmem. The _prep parameter appears to allow caching preprocessing for repeated searches of the same pattern.
requirements: _str must point to a memory block of at least n bytes; n must be non-negative.
_pat must point to a memory block of at least m bytes; m must be non-negative.
If m == 0, behavior is implementation-defined/unknown.
_prep may be NULL or point to a preprocessing cache; ownership/lifetime is not documented here (unknown).
Returns a pointer into _str where the first match starts, or NULL if not found; returned pointer must not be freed.

functions.name: kstrtok
functions.description: Tokenizes a string without modifying it, similar to strtok_r but non-destructive. Both str and sep can be NULL for subsequent calls when sep is unchanged. Returns a pointer to the start of the current token; the end of the token is provided via aux->p (aux->p points to the end of the current token).
requirements: aux must be a valid pointer to a ks_tokaux_t that persists across calls for a given tokenization sequence.

On the first call for a string, str should point to the input NUL-terminated string and sep to a NUL-terminated separator set; on subsequent calls, pass str==NULL and (for efficiency) sep==NULL if separators are unchanged.
Returned token is not NUL-terminated because the input is not modified; callers must use the range [return_value, aux->p) to access the token or copy it out.
str must remain valid for the duration of tokenization (no modification or deallocation between calls).

functions.name: kgetline
functions.description: Appends a line read via a supplied fgets-like function to the kstring_t s. Reads a line terminated by "\n" or "\r\n" and appends it to s without the line terminator. Returns 0 on successfully reading a line, or EOF at end-of-file or on error (as determined by the fgets-like function).
requirements: s must point to a valid, initialized kstring_t; existing content in s is preserved and the new line is appended.
fgets must be a function compatible with the signature char *(char *buf, int size, void *fp) that reads from the stream/context fp and returns NULL on EOF/error, similar to standard fgets.
fp is an opaque pointer passed through to the fgets-like function; it must reference a valid stream/context for that function.
Caller must check for EOF return to detect end-of-input or errors.
The underlying buffer may be reallocated; do not hold stale pointers to s->s across the call.

functions.name: ks_resize
functions.signature: static inline int ks_resize(kstring_t *s, size_t size);
functions.description: Ensures the kstring_t has capacity for at least size bytes, growing the buffer with realloc if needed. Does not change the current length s->l. Returns 0 on success or -1 on allocation failure.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a kstring_t; s may have s->s==NULL for initial allocation.
size is the required capacity (in bytes); function will round up internally.
On success, s->m is updated and s->s may be reallocated; callers must not rely on previous s->s after calling.
Caller must handle a -1 return indicating allocation failure.

functions.name: ks_str
functions.description: Returns the underlying char* buffer of the kstring_t. No allocation or modification is performed.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a kstring_t.
Returned pointer is owned by s and may be reallocated by subsequent kstring operations; do not free it directly unless you have taken ownership via ks_release().

functions.name: ks_len
functions.description: Returns the current length (number of bytes used) of the kstring_t’s content.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a kstring_t.
Length does not include any trailing NUL terminator.

functions.name: ks_release
functions.description: Releases ownership of the underlying buffer from the kstring_t and returns it to the caller. Resets s to an empty state (l = m = 0, s = NULL). The caller becomes responsible for freeing the returned buffer.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a kstring_t.
After return, s is empty and can be reused or allowed to go out of scope without leaking.
The returned pointer must be freed by the caller with free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: kputsn
functions.signature: static inline int kputsn(const char *p, int l, kstring_t *s);
functions.description: Appends l bytes from buffer p to the kstring_t s and NUL-terminates the string. Returns l on success, or EOF on allocation failure.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized kstring_t; its buffer may be reallocated.
p must point to at least l bytes of readable memory; l must be non-negative.
Caller must check for EOF return to detect allocation failure.
After success, s->s is NUL-terminated; s->l is increased by l.

functions.name: kputs
functions.signature: static inline int kputs(const char *p, kstring_t *s);
functions.description: Appends the NUL-terminated C string p to the kstring_t s and NUL-terminates the result. Returns the number of bytes appended (strlen(p)) on success, or EOF on allocation failure.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized kstring_t; its buffer may be reallocated.
p must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Caller must check for EOF return to detect allocation failure.

functions.name: kputc
functions.signature: static inline int kputc(int c, kstring_t *s);
functions.description: Appends a single byte c to the kstring_t s and NUL-terminates the string. Returns the character value c on success, or EOF on allocation failure.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized kstring_t; its buffer may be reallocated.
c is written as a single unsigned char (low 8 bits) value.
